summary.implementedScope: Gated the existing post-commit boundary-advance registration in intake's pipeline on a recorded turn_end (same registration site, ordering, and throw isolation); reshaped the boundary decision to whole-turn groups (turn_id-consecutive grouping, NULL as singleton) with the peek-ahead stop (evict only while remaining ≥ target) and protection for both the open turn's group and the newest remaining group; retired floorTokens from VisibilityBudgets with 64k/32k defaults, max > target validation, and rejection of unknown budget fields; applied the Epic 03 amendment ledger to view-boundary.test.ts and the G1 trajectory golden (re-cut for turn grouping), superseded the floor/monster-turn legs into the new TC-5.2 newest-turn-protection legs, added view-boundary-turn-end.test.ts covering TC-5.1–TC-5.3 including golden G2 (30k/25k/20k/15k under defaults landing the zone at 35k), and regenerated the red manifest. Story gate (verify) and epic gate (verify-all) both pass: 40 files, 376 passed, 9 env-gated skips.
summary.acceptanceRationale: Story-lead is pausing for caller ruling 06-turn-end-boundary-advance-story-run-001-ruling-020 before impl-lead can accept the story.

evidence: AC-5.3 still says the advance lands in `[target, target + one turn)`. The new trailing-turnless TC-5.2 leg in `view-boundary-turn-end.test.ts` uses budgets 100/60 with groups t1=50, newest closed t2=45, trailing turnless=70, then expects boundary after t1 and `zoneTokens` 115. If the next protected turn is the newest closed turn, the AC window is `[60, 105)`, so the expected 115 is outside it. This is not a code failure in the quick fix; it exposes a product/spec ruling needed for the legal trailing-turnless shape because a scalar boundary cannot both skip the trailing singleton and preserve the newest closed turn. The story technical notes were changed to protect trailing turnless singletons after the newest closed turn, but the AC wording and tech-design.md Flow 5 still carry the general landing-window phrasing.

rulingRequest.question: For zones where the newest closed turn is followed by trailing turnless singleton groups, should AC-5.3 allow an explicit exception to the `[target, target + one turn)` landing guarantee so newest-closed-turn protection and trailing-turnless protection remain authoritative?
rulingRequest.defaultRecommendation: Allow the explicit exception and update AC-5.3/tech-design wording to state that protected newest-closed-turn plus trailing turnless groups may leave the zone above `target + one turn`; keep the current implementation and tests, then rerun verification.
evidence: F-06-001 is resolved by code/test evidence, but F-06-002 remains blocking.
Verifier example: budgets 100/60 with groups t1=50, newest closed t2=45, trailing turnless=70 expects boundary after t1 and zoneTokens 115.
AC-5.3 says landing must be in [target, target + one turn); with target 60 and next protected turn 45, expected window is [60, 105), so 115 violates the literal window.
Story technical notes say newest closed turn and trailing turnless singletons after it are never candidates.
allowedResponses: Allow landing-window exception for protected trailing-turnless-after-newest-closed zones
Require trailing turnless singletons to be evictable to preserve the landing window
Reject both and block this story for a redesigned boundary model
